articles.title: India's October 2026 trade data: record exports, record imports, a 12-month-high merchandise deficit — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Exports are the headline, but the deficit and the oil bill are the real story. Merchandise exports jumped 45% y/y (fastest in five years) on petroleum-product re-exports and electronics, while crude at a 14-year-high price pushed the merchandise gap up. The services surplus cushions the *overall* deficit. Separate RBI data: Q2 current account deficit (Sept) $7.4 bn; H1 FY27 CAD $25.8 bn.
**Memorise:**
- Merchandise exports $49.47 bn (record, +45%); imports $89.35 bn (record, +16.5%); merchandise deficit $39.88 bn (12-month high).
- Services exports $40.51 bn, imports $20.72 bn (surplus ~$19.79 bn); overall (goods + services) deficit $20.1 bn vs $25.1 bn a year ago.
- Crude imports +54% to $22.82 bn (Indian basket $119.91/bbl, 14-year high); petroleum-product exports ~doubled to $8.89 bn; gold imports −63% to $5.51 bn; electronics imports $14.32 bn, exports $6.64 bn.
- April–October FY27: exports $309.06 bn, imports $527.21 bn, merchandise deficit $218.15 bn. September CAD $7.4 bn; overall BoP surplus $8.8 bn; H1 CAD $25.8 bn. ICRA sees FY27 CAD ~0.9% of GDP.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (External sector).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal / Ramesh Singh — *Balance of Payments*: current account = merchandise trade + invisibles (services, income, transfers). *Nudge:* add an "Oct 2026" row to your BoP data card and a cross-link to "oil price shock → CAD → rupee (₹94.25/$ on 13 Nov)".

articles.title: Matsya-6000: India's crewed deep-ocean submersible heads for its first 500 m dive — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Flagship of the Deep Ocean Mission's Samudrayaan project. Useful for "technology development" and ocean-resources (polymetallic nodules) questions. Per the report dated 14 Nov, the first 500 m trial dive is now planned for Jan–Feb 2027 in the Bay of Bengal (earlier plans slipped; the manned 6,000 m dive is a later milestone).
**Memorise:**
- Developed by NIOT (Chennai, MoES) with ISRO support for the titanium hull.
- Crew of 3; titanium-alloy sphere 2.1 m diameter, 80 mm thick, designed for ~600 bar; rated depth 6,000 m.
- Samudrayaan launched 2021; Deep Ocean Mission outlay ~₹4,077 crore over five years (as reported).
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (ocean technology); GS1 Geography (ocean resources).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Spectrum — ocean resources (polymetallic nodules, hydrothermal sulphides, ISA licences in the Indian Ocean). *Nudge:* add a "Deep Ocean Mission — six pillars" cross-link under Sci-Tech ‘Indigenous missions’.

articles.title: Ministry of Electronics & IT: Semicon 2.0 application portal launched; 12 more ECMS projects approved (5–6 Nov 2026; PIB-based coverage) — GS3 Economy / Sci-Tech *(not covered before: the 30 Oct briefing carried only the earlier ECMS tranche)*
articles.text:
**What & why it matters:** Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw launched a web portal for applications under the Semicon India Programme (Semicon 2.0, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0). It covers the machines and materials, new fabs and ATMP/OSAT pillars. He also announced 12 more approvals under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), which aims to move India from downstream assembly to a domestic components value chain.

**Key facts:**
- The 12 new ECMS projects carry proposed investment of ₹7,503 crore, expected production of ₹39,045 crore and about 7,127 direct jobs (PTI report).
- Cumulative ECMS: 118 applications across 16 states and 34 products; investment ₹77,051 crore; projected production ₹5.73 lakh crore; about 81,755 direct jobs (PTI). Nearly half of the approved units are MSMEs (Drishti, citing PIB).
- Semicon 2.0 outlay is reported as ₹1,27,500 crore, with six pillars: chip design, machines and materials, fabs, ATMP/OSAT, R&D and talent (reports; Cabinet approval reported as July 2026, which I could not verify on PIB).
- Components covered include multi-layer PCBs, relays, heat sinks, specialty ceramics, copper foil, battery materials and precision tooling.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (ITPO): 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, Bharat Mandapam (inaugurated 13 Nov by Piyush Goyal; 14–27 Nov) — GS3 Economy / Trade
articles.text:
**What & why it matters:** India's largest annual trade fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO). It showcases state economies, ODOP products and start-ups, and links to export promotion and "Vocal for Local".

**Key facts:** Theme "Vikas aur Virasat". Business (B2B) days 14–18 Nov; public days 19–27 Nov. Over 3,500 exhibitors in 17 halls. Partner States: Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Focus States: Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal. 32 States/UTs and 51 central bodies participate, plus 11 country pavilions and about 600 start-ups at the Hall of Inspiration (single secondary source).

articles.title: Department of Science & Technology / Indian Institute of Astrophysics: COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium inaugurated by the PM (13 Nov 2026) — GS3 Science & Technology
articles.text:
**What & why it matters:** Billed as India's first LED-dome planetarium, built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) with the University of Mysore at the foot of Chamundi Hill. It is a tool for science popularisation and scientific temper.

**Key facts:** Tilted 15 m dome, over 6,000 LED panels, 8K visuals (about 42 megapixels) and no projector; seats 168; shows in Kannada, English and Hindi. In his speech the PM cited the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, the "One Nation One Subscription" scheme for research journals, and over 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs (single secondary source).

articles.title: Ministry of Education (Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan): Three digital initiatives launched — Vidya Samiksha Kendra with AI "Samiksha" bot, KVS-Samvaad parent app, KVS Alumni Connect portal (reported 14 Nov 2026; *single source — verify the launching minister and details on PIB*) — GS2 Governance / Education
articles.text:
**What & why it matters:** Data-driven school management (AI analysis of school data), parent engagement (attendance, results, communication) and alumni networking. Relevant to the digital-governance theme in NEP implementation.

### Also worth a line (not independently verified on PIB)
- ISRO ran a ground static test of an upgraded PSLV third-stage solid motor (PS3) at Sriharikota, with a revised nozzle and stronger sealing, after anomalies in recent PSLV missions.
- IMNEX-26: 8th India–Myanmar naval exercise at Visakhapatnam, 10–14 Nov.
- NPCI's UPI Vyapaar Saksham scheme for small merchants in Tier III–VI cities and special regions, funded by 5% of UPI MDR once MDR is implemented (not yet notified).

### Scheme-in-focus: Semicon India Programme 2.0 and the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)
- **Ministry:** MeitY (India Semiconductor Mission). **Objective:** build an end-to-end domestic semiconductor and electronics-components ecosystem and cut import dependence.
- **Key features:** (1) Semicon 2.0 pillars on equipment and materials, fabs and ATMP/OSAT, alongside design, R&D and talent; (2) ECMS incentivises components and sub-assemblies (PCBs, relays, ceramics, battery materials) and capital goods; (3) a single online application portal to speed up approvals; (4) a large MSME share among approved units.
- **Coverage:** 118 ECMS projects in 16 states (reported). **Significance:** supply-chain resilience, Atmanirbhar Bharat, jobs and the "India as an electronics hub" strategy; link to PLI reviews (see the CA briefing of 14 Nov for the PLI assessment).

articles.title: NITI Aayog–IIM Ahmedabad assessment: only 18.5% of PLI outlay disbursed so far — Economy / Reports
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** PLI is the flagship manufacturing-push tool (Atmanirbhar Bharat). The assessment shows a gap between investment/production outcomes and incentive payouts, and that MSME benefits are largely indirect (via supply chains of anchor firms). Good for GS3 "industrial policy" and "inclusive growth" answers.
**Key facts:** 14 sectors; outlay ~₹1.91 lakh crore; incentives disbursed ₹35,354 cr (18.5%) till March 2026; investment ₹2.4 trn (76% of target); production ₹22.66 trn (64%); jobs ~8.49 lakh (~28% of ~30.2 lakh target). White goods best MSME case (domestic value addition ~20% FY20 → 55% FY25). Report says PLI "never designed primarily" for MSMEs.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Industry).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh / Shankar IAS "Industrial Policy & Manufacturing" → update with this assessment; cross-link to *Make in India*, MSME definition, and Economic Survey chapter on manufacturing.

articles.title: Global Carbon Budget 2026: global fossil CO₂ dips, India's set to rise 4.4% — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Prelims-friendly report (who publishes, key numbers) and a Mains hook on India's "industry-led" emissions growth while the power sector flattens, linked to NDC and COP31 negotiations.
**Key facts:** 21st edition by the **Global Carbon Project** (journal *Earth System Science Data*). Fossil CO₂ projected −0.4% to 38.2 Gt in 2026; total incl. land use ~43.3 Gt; ~150 Gt CO₂ left for 1.5°C ("<4 years" at current rates); China −0.9%, US −1.3%, EU −1.5%, **India +4.4%**. CO₂ ~427.7 ppm. (CREA, as reported: India's H1 2026 CO₂ +3.7%, led by steel and cement.)
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (Climate change).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Climate Change" chapter → add GCB to the "reports & institutions" table (GCP vs IPCC vs UNEP vs WMO); India's NDC (45% intensity cut by 2030 vs 2005; net zero 2070).

articles.title: First BIMSTEC Health Ministers' Meeting, Colombo (11 Nov) — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** BIMSTEC is India's preferred platform under "Neighbourhood First/Act East" while SAARC is dormant; functional cooperation (health, traditional medicine, digital) is a soft-power tool.
**Key facts:** Joint Ministerial Statement and revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–30) adopted; **BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine to be hosted at ITRA, Jamnagar (Gujarat)**; proposed BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework; AMR and pandemic preparedness listed as priorities; India–Sri Lanka MoU for 100 ambulances (grant ~USD 5.28 mn) and support for 50 health kiosks; next ministerial meeting in Thailand, 2028 (biennial). Seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations.

articles.title: ISRO fires revised PSLV third stage (PS3) at Sriharikota (12 Nov) — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Return-to-flight diligence after third-stage anomalies on PSLV-C61/EOS-09 (May 2025) and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 (Jan 2026). Tests understanding of launch-vehicle staging and reliability engineering.
**Key facts:** Ground static test at the Static Test Facility, SDSC-SHAR; changes include improved nozzle design margins, **redundant sealing**, strengthened interfaces, and revised raw-material acceptance, assembly and non-destructive testing; ISRO will review data and conduct further tests (no launch date announced). PS3 is a solid motor (reported max thrust ~240 kN).
**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (Space).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum/Shankar IAS "Space Technology" → add PSLV stage table (PS1 solid, PS2 liquid, PS3 solid, PS4 liquid); cross-link to SSLV, NSIL and IN-SPACe.

articles.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals (Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers): PLI scheme for Medical Devices extended to 2035-36 with ~₹2,700 crore; fresh applications invited (reported 10–11 Nov 2026) — GS3 Economy / Industry / Health
articles.text:
- **What:** The PLI scheme for medical devices (launched 2020-21) is extended by eight years with a revised outlay of about ₹2,700 crore, eligibility norms eased, and a new online application portal.
- **Why it matters:** Reduces import dependence in medtech and deepens domestic manufacturing of critical components and advanced devices.
- **Key facts:** Four segments — (i) consumables, disposables and implants; (ii) critical components; (iii) advanced devices with limited domestic manufacturing; (iv) high-end equipment currently only assembled in India. Average incentive ≈5% / 9% / 6% by segment (reported); minimum sales threshold for claiming incentives dropped; minimum investment lowered (earlier ₹180 crore; new figure not confirmed); three years to set up production. Original scheme reportedly supported 60+ devices/components and >₹16,000 crore output.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (industrial policy, PLI), Health.

articles.title: Ministry of External Affairs: Inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, New Delhi (20–22 Nov 2026) — invitations confirmed by MEA spokesperson, 13 Nov *(single secondary source; verify)* — GS2 International Relations
articles.text:
- **What:** India-proposed forum on cultural exchange and people-to-people ties across Eurasia; all 10 SCO members (including Pakistan) invited, plus observers and dialogue partners.
- **Why it matters:** Soft-power / civilisational diplomacy within the SCO; India's first such forum while Pakistan holds the SCO Council of Heads of State chair (2026–27).
- **Key facts:** SCO members: Belarus, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan (India full member since 2017). Observers include Afghanistan and Mongolia; 15 dialogue partners.
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR (regional groupings).

### Scheme-in-focus: PLI Scheme for Medical Devices (PLI-MD 2.0)

- **Name / Ministry:** PLI Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices — Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers.
- **Objective:** Build domestic medtech manufacturing capacity and cut import dependence.
- **Key features:** (1) Extended to FY 2035-36, outlay ≈₹2,700 crore; (2) four target segments from consumables to high-end equipment; (3) incentive on incremental sales, with minimum sales threshold removed and investment threshold lowered; (4) three-year gestation to set up plants; online portal for fresh applications.
- **Beneficiaries/coverage:** Domestic and foreign medical-device manufacturers setting up in India.
- **Significance:** Part of the broader PLI architecture (pharma, bulk drugs, medical devices) under Atmanirbhar Bharat.

### Also worth a line (not verified on PIB)
- Public Service Broadcasting Day (12 Nov) marks Mahatma Gandhi's 1947 live AIR broadcast.
- India–Sri Lanka healthcare MoU (100 ambulances, 50 medical kiosks/Health ATMs) reported alongside the BIMSTEC health meeting (already covered 12 Nov).

articles.title: Retail inflation hits 6.09% in October 2026, breaching RBI's upper tolerance band — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** CPI (new series, base 2024=100) rose to 6.09% from 5.54% in September, the first breach of the 6% ceiling in about two years and the highest on the new series. Food inflation (CFPI) was 8.94% (7.74% in September), driven by onion (+116%), garlic, ginger and lemon; potato and cauliflower prices fell. This tests the flexible inflation-targeting (FIT) framework: target 4% ±2% retained for 1 Apr 2026–31 Mar 2031. A breach alone does not trigger the formal failure clause, which needs three consecutive quarters outside the band.
**Memorise:** CPI Oct 2026 6.09%; rural 6.63%, urban 5.41%; CFPI 8.94%; band 2–6%; failure = 3 consecutive quarters → RBI report to the Government.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Inflation & Monetary Policy).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal/Ramesh Singh "Inflation & Monetary Policy" pillar. *Nudge:* add the Oct-2026 data point and the 2026–31 target period to your FIT note; cross-link to MPC composition.

articles.title: SC: cultivation alone does not make one a "forest dweller" under FRA (A. John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu, 6 Nov) — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta held that people who cultivate forest land but only reside temporarily in the forest, or live outside its boundary, cannot qualify as Forest Dwelling STs (s.2(c)) or Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (s.2(o)) on cultivation alone; planned commercial-crop cultivation is prima facie not a recognised right. The Court set up a Special Committee headed by former CJI B.R. Gavai to scrutinise FRA claim orders, and directed the State to constitute the remaining Gram Sabhas in 30 days. Good for Mains: balancing tribal rights, forest conservation and administrative delay.
**Memorise:** 2026 INSC 1204; FRA 2006; ss.2(c), 2(o); Special Committee under ex-CJI Gavai; 30 days for Gram Sabhas, then 5 months for adjudication.
**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance (also GS1 Society, GS3 Environment).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS Environment "Forest Rights Act"; Laxmikanth "Scheduled and Tribal Areas". *Nudge:* add this judgment under FRA case law and cross-link to the Gram Sabha's role.

articles.title: India rejects US court order on serving NSA Doval and ex-RAW chief in Pannun civil suit — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 9 Nov, Judge Katherine Polk Failla (SDNY) allowed the plaintiff to pursue alternative service on NSA Ajit Doval and former RAW chief Samant Goel through Delhi courts under Article 19 of the Hague Service Convention; the service packet is due by 30 Nov. MEA (10 Nov) rejected "fabricated and malicious attacks" and said service requests must go through the Ministry of Law and Justice. The order does not mean anyone has been served or establishes liability. Raises sovereign immunity, extraterritorial jurisdiction and India–US trust issues.
**Memorise:** SDNY, 9 Nov 2026; Hague Service Convention Art. 19; deadline 30 Nov; Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty in Feb 2026 (does not establish the civil allegations).
**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal/Vision "India–US relations" pillar. *Nudge:* add a "legal-diplomatic friction" sub-heading with the sovereign-immunity argument.

articles.title: TDB commits ₹64.05 crore from RDI Fund for Astrome's AI-enabled ELINT satellite constellation (12 Nov) — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Technology Development Board (DST) will fund Astrome Technologies (Bengaluru) through Optionally Convertible Debt, against a total project cost of ₹128.11 crore, to build a "sovereign space-based intelligence system": ~50-kg microsatellites in LEO with an ELINT payload, AI-based ground processing and inter-satellite links. Links the RDI Fund (private-sector deep-tech financing), space-sector reforms and defence ISR self-reliance. Know TRL-4 → TRL-9.
**Memorise:** ₹64.05 cr of ₹128.11 cr; OCD; TRL-4→9; ~50 kg microsatellites; ELINT = non-communication signals (e.g. radar).
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Space) and Internal Security.
**Static anchor:** Spectrum/Vision "Space Technology"; Mrunal "Space sector reforms". *Nudge:* add ELINT vs COMINT vs SIGINT definitions and the RDI Fund line.

articles.title: India prohibits export of lithium-ion battery "black mass" (DGFT, 10 Nov) — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** DGFT moved black mass (ITC-HS 85491400) from "Free" to "Prohibited" with immediate effect, to keep lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese feedstock at home. Recycling capacity above 60,000 tonnes a year is under-utilised for want of feedstock. Complements the National Critical Mineral Mission and the ₹1,500-crore recycling incentive scheme (Sept 2025); follows the 6 Nov news on solar/wind recycling guidelines — a circular-economy and resource-security cluster.
**Memorise:** Notification 10 Nov 2026; HS 85491400; Li, Co, Ni, Mn; DGFT is under the Commerce Ministry.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment / Economy (Critical Minerals).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Waste Management"; Mrunal "Critical Minerals". *Nudge:* add a "Battery recycling" box and cross-link to the Battery Waste Management framework.

articles.title: Cabinet approves ₹62,370 crore NBS subsidy for Rabi 2026-27 (11 Nov) — Agriculture / Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) fixes a per-kg subsidy on nutrients, not on products, and covers P&K fertilisers, not urea. This year the government blames West Asia and Russia–Ukraine price shocks, so the subsidy bill is overshooting the budget.
**Facts to memorize:**
- Period 1 Oct 2026–31 Mar 2027, about ₹24,418 crore more than Rabi 2025-26.
- Rates per kg of nutrient: N ₹94.21, P ₹66.11, S ₹10.42, K ₹2.38 (unchanged).
- DAP retail price held at ₹1,350 per 50-kg bag; SSP freight subsidy continues as a DAP substitute.
- Support for domestic sulphur and sulphuric acid: 20% of procurement cost.
- Total P&K subsidy for 2026-27 is ₹1,03,903 crore, against roughly ₹54,000 crore budgeted for NBS.

**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture / Economy.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Agriculture pillar (fertiliser subsidy) and Shankar IAS Agriculture chapter. *Update:* add the 2026-27 NBS figures and cross-link to the Fiscal Deficit / Subsidies notes.

articles.title: PM to visit Manila (16–18 Nov) for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Announced by Secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon at the 12 Nov MEA briefing. ASEAN engagement is framed as a "building block" of Act East, and the Indo-Pacific/maritime link is stressed. The Philippines is the 2026 ASEAN chair.
**Facts to memorize:**
- 23rd ASEAN-India Summit; 21st EAS process meeting (ASEAN-led, eight leaders).
- Theme of ASEAN 2026: "Navigating the Future".
- Dinner by President Marcos Jr., bilaterals on the sidelines; India is an EAS member but not an ASEAN member.

**Notebook:** GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar (Act East / ASEAN). *Update:* add the 23rd Summit and EAS numbering; cross-link to Quad/Indo-Pacific notes. Verify the outcomes after 18 Nov.

articles.title: Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 awards presented (11 Nov) — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The 10th edition of the world's largest cleanliness survey, run by MoHUA, links urban governance with waste management. Prelims asks about the survey's nodal ministry and its link to SBM-Urban.
**Facts to memorize:**
- Awards presented by the President on 11 Nov 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
- 43 indicators across 10 areas: waste segregation, collection and disposal, sanitation, used water management, citizen engagement.
- Winners were not confirmed in the sources I could verify; add them from PIB.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment / GS2 Urban Governance.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS Environment (Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016) and Laxmikanth, Municipalities chapter (12th Schedule). *Update:* add the 10th-edition details and the winners list.

articles.title: Union Cabinet (Dept of Fertilizers): Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for Rabi 2026-27 approved — ~₹62,370 crore (11 Nov 2026) — GS3 Agriculture / Economy
articles.text:
- **What:** The Cabinet approved NBS rates on Phosphatic & Potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the Rabi season, applicable **1 Oct 2026 – 31 Mar 2027**. Briefed by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.
- **Why it matters:** Budgetary requirement of about **₹62,370.02 crore** is roughly **₹24,418 crore (~64%) higher** than Rabi 2025-26 (₹37,952.29 crore) and well above Kharif 2026 (~₹41,534 crore), reflecting high global prices of DAP, MOP, sulphur and inputs. The Government says farmers will not bear extra burden and domestic manufacturing will rise.
- **Key facts:** NBS in force since **1 April 2010**; **28 P&K grades** subsidised; urea is outside NBS (statutory MRP, separate subsidy).
- **Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture (inputs, subsidies), Economy (fiscal burden of subsidies).
- *Ministry note: sources did not name the ministry; NBS is administered by the Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers (static knowledge).*

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: First BIMSTEC Health Ministers' Meeting, Colombo (10–11 Nov 2026) — GS2 International Relations / Health
articles.text:
- **What:** Union Minister J.P. Nadda represented India. Members adopted a **Joint Ministerial Statement** and the **Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030)** covering surveillance, pandemic preparedness, digital health, traditional medicine, One Health and health workforce.
- **Key facts:** India to host the **BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar** and the next Task Force on Traditional Medicine meeting; a **BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework** (telemedicine, interoperable records, AI diagnostics) to be explored; ministers to meet **every two years**, Thailand to host the second in **2028**. Meeting follows the 6th BIMSTEC Summit (Bangkok, April 2025). India–Sri Lanka: MoU for **100 ambulances** (~US$5.28 m grant) and support for **50 health kiosks** under the post-Cyclone Ditwah rehabilitation package.
- **Members:** Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR (neighbourhood-first, BIMSTEC), GS2 Health.

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (NCAHP): Draft rules on provisional registration of allied & healthcare professionals (released ~9–11 Nov 2026; comments reportedly till 4 Dec — one source) — GS2 Governance / Health
articles.text:
- **What:** The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has issued draft provisions to bring practitioners **without recognised qualifications** into the regulated system.
- **Key features:** (1) **Provisional registration** with the State Allied & Healthcare Council (NCAHP directly where no council exists), valid **3 years, extendable by 1**; (2) **bridge courses** of 6–12 months with supervised clinical training; (3) a **qualifying exam** to obtain full registration within three years; (4) covers trades across **10 broad categories** (physiotherapy, optometry, lab technology, psychology, dietetics etc.). Draft only — not final.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance (regulation of health workforce), GS2 Health (NCAHP Act, 2021).

articles.title: Cabinet (11 Nov) extends CGFMU (Mudra guarantee) and Stand-Up India to 2031 — Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Credit guarantees de-risk lending to micro units and first-generation entrepreneurs without direct subsidy. Guarantee fee cuts and a higher loan ceiling signal a push on formal credit for the informal sector (GS3 inclusive growth; MSME finance).
- **Key facts:** CGFMU continued for 5 years to 31 Mar 2031; corpus ₹5,000 crore backing PMMY loans of ₹12.6 lakh crore; guarantee fee cut 1% → 0.75%; cover for PMMY loans up to ₹20 lakh; also ₹10,000 Jan Dhan overdrafts and ₹10–20 lakh SHG loans; run by NCGTC. PMMY so far: 60.36 crore loans, ₹43.34 lakh crore (Sep 2026). **Stand-Up India** (launched Apr 2016) extended to 31 Mar 2031: corpus ₹4,111 crore; loans above ₹10 lakh up to ₹1 crore for Women/SC/ST greenfield enterprises; guarantee up to 85%, fee 0.50%; target 2.5 lakh more entrepreneurs.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Inclusive growth / MSME).
- **Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh, Banking & Financial Inclusion; Mrunal Economy "Credit & Financial Inclusion". *Nudge:* add CGFMU–Stand-Up–CGTMSE as a comparison table (corpus, fee, ceiling).

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah's first bilateral visit to India (reported 22–24 Nov) — International Relations
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Neighbourhood First reset with Nepal's new government (in office since 27 Mar 2026, per press reports); connectivity, energy, flood-relief diplomacy.
- **Key facts:** MEA (10 Nov): "entire range" of ties to be discussed; dates still being worked out officially. Foreign Secretary Misri met PM Shah in Kathmandu (4–5 Nov): energy, water, trade, transit, aviation. Ayodhya–Janakpur rail service trial run held 5 Nov; Shah thanked India for Rasuwa–Bhotekoshi flood relief. No agreements signed yet; reports expect an assistance package and agreements during the visit.
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR (Neighbourhood).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Vajiram IR notes: India–Nepal (1950 Treaty, Sugauli 1816, Kalapani). *Nudge:* add a 2026 timeline box.

articles.title: IIT-Jodhpur's niobium-based Refractory Complex Lean Alloy (RCLA) — Science & Technology
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Indigenous advanced materials for hypersonic, rocket and re-entry systems: self-reliance in strategic technology (Atmanirbharta in defence/space).
- **Key facts:** Density ~7.6 g/cm³ (vs ~9–10 for C-103/WC3009); after 24 h at 1,000°C gained 43.48 mg/cm² vs 258 mg/cm² for C-103, no pesting; room-temperature yield strength 1.13 GPa; ~29% compressive strain; "Complex Lean Alloy" design approach; led by Dr Saurabh Nene; made and tested at IIT-Jodhpur without foreign help.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech.

articles.text:

- **Adaptation:** supports voluntary indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation, not as conditions for finance.
- **Just Transition Work Programme** to continue; technology transfer is a developed-country obligation; carbon-market participation voluntary.
- Coalitions: G-77 & China, LMDC, BASIC. Side events: LeadIT 3.0 (with Sweden), International Big Cat Alliance, coastal resilience.

articles.title: SC holds National Book Trust is "State" under Article 12 (reported 6 Nov) — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** In *Chairman, National Book Trust India v. A.R. Abdul Gaffar* a Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Augustine George Masih — dismissed the NBT's appeal and upheld the Delhi High Court: a society formed by government resolution is "State" where government control is deep and pervasive. The Court applied the cumulative financial–functional–administrative test (*Ajay Hasia*, *Pradeep Kumar Biswas*) and held that registration as a society and some self-earned revenue do not take a body out of Art. 12. It also drew limits: performing public functions alone does not make a body "State", and NBT staff do not become civil servants (no Arts. 309–311 protection).
**Memorise:** Government appoints the NBT Chairman and nominates governing-body members; CAG audits it; consequence = fundamental rights (Part III) are enforceable against it (writ jurisdiction, Art. 32/226). Landmarks: *Rajasthan SEB v. Mohan Lal* (1967, "other authorities"), *Ajay Hasia* (1981), *Pradeep Kumar Biswas v. IICB* (2002, "pervasive control").
**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance (Fundamental Rights, Judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — *Fundamental Rights* → Art. 12 "State"; Shankar IAS — Fundamental Rights. *Nudge:* add "NBT (2026)" as a worked example under the Pradeep Kumar Biswas test and cross-link to Art. 309–311.

articles.title: Aditya-L1's VELC finds a solar eruption expanded asymmetrically (study reported 4–5 Nov) — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) observed on 5 Aug 2024 by the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) did not expand as a symmetric bubble; two Doppler-shifted emission branches on opposite sides of the line showed plasma moving towards and away from the observer. Combining VELC spectra with NASA SDO images and 3D modelling, the study shows VELC can constrain a CME's 3D geometry from a single vantage point. Why it matters: CME shape affects drag and hence Earth-arrival-time forecasts (space weather).
**Memorise:** Authors from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru (Tripathi, Samanta, Joshi); published in *The Astrophysical Journal Letters*; VELC observations covered 1.05–1.5 solar radii. Aditya-L1: launched 2 Sep 2023 (PSLV-C57), placed in a halo orbit around Sun–Earth L1 (~1.5 million km) on 6 Jan 2024; seven payloads.
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Space).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS/Mrunal — Space technology (India's missions); NCERT Class 11–12 Physics (Sun, magnetic fields; Physics optional: solar physics/plasma). *Nudge:* add a "space weather: CME, solar flare, geomagnetic storm" box next to Aditya-L1 payload list.

articles.title: Ministry of Science & Technology / MEA (with European Commission): India–EU conclude negotiations on India's association with Horizon Europe (announced 6–7 Nov 2026) — GS3 Sci-Tech / GS2 IR
articles.text:
- **What:** Negotiations for India to become an *Associated Country* of Horizon Europe, the EU's research & innovation framework programme (2021–2027, budget ~€93.5 billion), have concluded. Exploratory talks began Feb 2026; formal talks July 2026. Formal agreement is expected to be signed around Jan 2027, subject to procedures on both sides.
- **Why it matters:** Indian researchers, institutions and industry can bid for funding and lead collaborative projects (notably under Pillar II, "Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness": health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, bioeconomy) on equal terms with EU counterparts, in return for a financial contribution to the programme. Complements the India–EU Trade & Technology Council and FTA push.
- **Key facts:** Horizon Europe 2021–27; €93.5 bn; association agreement ~Jan 2027; reciprocal access to research infrastructure.

articles.title: Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals: PIB Backgrounder — India's chemicals sector and the three operational PCPIRs (7 Nov 2026)* — GS3 Economy / Industry
articles.text:

Most chemical sub-sectors permit 100% FDI via the automatic route; the RDI scheme is open to chemicals; Budget 2026 announced a ₹600 crore chemical-parks scheme with three dedicated clusters. Major Accident Hazard (MAH) workforce-training programme under Viksit Bharat@2047 plan targets all 2,393 MAH units over 5 years.

articles.title: UPI MDR: NPCI defends the revised framework before the Supreme Court — Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** *Only the new development here.* In its counter-affidavit NPCI says MDR is needed to sustain UPI's cost (infrastructure, security, fraud prevention), that merchants cannot pass it to customers, that it is a commercial fee and not a tax, and that NPCI is not "State" under Article 12. The Court had earlier (28 Sep) declined a stay and issued notice to the Centre, RBI and NPCI. The framework's start (originally 15 Oct) has been postponed.
- **Memorize:** Finance Ministry notification of 14 Sep 2026: zero charge on RuPay debit cards and UPI up to ₹2,000. P2P is free at any amount. For eligible P2M payments above ₹2,000 the MDR is capped at 0.4% (max ₹300); flat ₹5 for essential/thin-margin sectors. Merchants with monthly inward credits up to ₹1 lakh are exempt. P2P is 37% of UPI volume and 70% of value; about 4% of P2M transactions attract MDR. NPCI relies on Sections 20–21 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007; a small-merchant fund would take 5% of each entity's MDR share.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (payments, fintech).
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal, *Banking → Payment systems* (PSS Act 2007, RBI as the designated authority, NPCI as a not-for-profit Section 8 company). Update the "Zero-MDR 2020 → 2026 reversal" note in your UPI notes.

articles.title: Ministry of Home Affairs: Martyrs' Memorial ("Azadi ki Pehli Ladai ka Shaheed Smarak") of the 1857 Revolt inaugurated, Ambala Cantonment (5 Nov 2026) — GS1 Modern History / Art & Culture

articles.title: SC: the 24-hour clock under Article 22(2) runs from detention, not formal arrest (5 Nov) — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** In *Sujit Das v. Union of India*, the Court held that the "arrest" vs "detention" distinction is constitutionally unsustainable. A person curtailed of liberty must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours of that moment. Magistrates must record the actual time of detention and refuse remand if the limit was breached.
- **Memorize:** Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar. Four NDPS accused (11.03 kg yaba tablets) were detained at 2 PM on 29 Sep 2025 and shown as arrested at 11 AM on 30 Sep, about 18 hours later. Only travel time to the Magistrate is excludable. The Court disapproved the Orissa and Kerala HC and Madras HC views that excluded pre-arrest detention. BNSS Sections 56 and 58 were referred to.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Polity (Fundamental Rights).
- **Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Fundamental Rights* → Article 22 (rights of arrested persons; 22(3) exceptions). Add this case beside D.K. Basu and Arnesh Kumar, and cross-link it to the BNSS custody provisions.

articles.title: National Urbanisation Policy debate: Census 2027 will retain the 2011 urban-classification criteria — Geography / Society
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The first Census in 16 years keeps the old definition of "census town", which can undercount urbanisation. The Economic Survey 2026, Union Budget and 16th Finance Commission all point to the same gap: growth spills beyond municipal limits. Ties neatly to the 74th Amendment, municipal finance and airshed-level governance (over 65% of Delhi's winter PM2.5 originates outside the city).
**Memorise:** Census 2011: 377 million urban residents. Census town = population ≥5,000 + density ≥400/sq km + ≥75% male main workers in non-agricultural work. Peri-urban growth 4.15% p.a. vs 2.9% in core areas. ~52% of statutory towns and ~76% of census towns lack master plans. Municipal revenue ≈1% of GDP; property tax ≈0.15%. 16th FC: ₹10,000 crore "urbanisation premium" (to encourage merging peri-urban villages with municipalities). Budget 2026: ₹5,000 crore for City Economic Regions. UN: ~44% urban, >720 million by 2050.
**Notebook:** GS1 — Urbanisation/Geography; GS2 — Local governance.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — *Urban Local Government* (74th Amendment, Part IXA, Arts 243P–243ZG, Twelfth Schedule); Spectrum/NCERT — Human Settlements. *Nudge:* add a comparison table "Census town vs statutory town" and a cross-link to Smart Cities/AMRUT.

articles.title: Ministry of Earth Sciences (National Centre for Seismology): Seismological observatory inaugurated at Kishtwar, J&K (~2 Nov 2026) — GS1 Geography / GS3 Disaster Management
articles.text:

articles.title: Ganga Water Treaty nears expiry; MEA points to the Joint Rivers Commission (3 Nov briefing) — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The 1996 India–Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty expires in December 2026 (reported 12 Dec). MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said both countries have a "structured system" and an established mechanism, the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC), to discuss water sharing. No renewal-talk dates have been announced; India has reportedly invited Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman to visit New Delhi. Renewal is a test of neighbourhood diplomacy, with Teesta still unresolved.
**Memorize:**
- Signed 1996 by H.D. Deve Gowda and Sheikh Hasina; 30-year term (static knowledge).
- Governs dry-season Ganga flows at Farakka; JRC set up in 1972 (static knowledge).
- Teesta sharing is a separate, unsigned issue.
- Not verified: Bangladesh's formal position on renewal.

**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations (Neighbourhood).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS *India–Bangladesh relations*; Mrunal *Water diplomacy*. Update: add the expiry date to the treaty timeline and cross-link to Teesta and the Indus Waters Treaty.

articles.title: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways with Government of Bihar: MoU on the "Nadi Sanjeevani" initiative — desilting rivers and using silt in National Highway construction (signed New Delhi, 3 Nov 2026) — GS3 Environment / Infrastructure
articles.text:

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (with DGFT): Guwahati airport approved as an export point for agarwood chips and oil (31 Oct 2026) — GS3 Economy/Environment
articles.text:
- **What:** Lokapriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, has been approved as an export point for agarwood chips and oil. Assam holds about 81% of agarwood resources, per the report.
- **Why it matters:** Agarwood (Aquilaria spp.) is a CITES-listed (Appendix II) species, so exports need designated ports, permits and traceable supply chains. A designated North-East point cuts transit to other ports.
- **Background (verified):** The Centre released a *Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from the North Eastern Region* on 11 Aug 2026 (MDoNER with CHEMEXCIL). India has about 139.89 million agarwood trees; the North-East has 96%+ (Assam ~114.3 million, Tripura ~15.15 million). An Agarwood Cluster Development Project (Assam, Tripura; PM-DevINE) and an Agarwood International Trade and Research Centre in Agartala (NEC schemes) are in the pipeline; an Export Promotion Cell was formed in May 2026.
- *The airport approval is from a single secondary source; the Aug roadmap is from a news report on the summit.*

articles.title: Supreme Court sends the Reliance–Government KG basin gas dispute to mediation — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** the case is a long arbitration-versus-court contest. In 2018 an international tribunal, by a 2–1 majority, rejected the Government's USD 1.55 bn claim that Reliance, BP and Niko drew gas from deposits they had no right to exploit, and awarded the companies USD 8.3 m. The Delhi High Court (14 Feb 2025) set aside a single-judge ruling that had upheld the award. The Supreme Court, hearing the appeals, is reported by LiveLaw's 30 Oct blog to have referred the dispute to mediation.
**Memorize:**
- Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provides for setting aside an award.
- Mediation Act, 2023 institutionalises mediation.
- Courts encourage settlement but retain jurisdiction.

*Verification note:* the mediation reference rests on a live blog with possibly garbled text; other reports say the bench had earlier declined a stay of the hearing. Treat the final order as to be confirmed.
**Notebook:** GS2 Polity / Governance (judiciary, ADR).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter, plus the Arbitration Act and Mediation Act 2023 note. Cross-link to Article 136 (special leave).

articles.text:

articles.title: Ministry of Law & Justice (23rd Law Commission of India): National Conference on Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms, New Delhi (inaugurated by Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan; ~22 Oct 2026)
articles.text:

**Key facts:** Organised by the 23rd Law Commission; Union Law & Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal present; themes — law reforms, co-operative federalism, constitutional governance, institutional frameworks for administration of justice. The Law Commission is a **non-statutory, executive-constituted advisory body** (constituted for fixed terms by the Government via gazette notification). articles.title: Draft lab-animal rules, 2026: 3Rs, registration and Institutional Animal Ethics Committees — Environment (Animal Welfare)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A draft rule-making story that links the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 with Article 51A(g) (compassion for living creatures). Animal-rights groups such as PETA India have asked for withdrawal, arguing it weakens oversight. Good for "Statements" MCQs on regulators and committees.
**Key facts:**
- Issued by the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying** on **6 Oct 2026** as **G.S.R. 864(E)**; comments invited until **6 Nov 2026**.
- Built on the **3Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement**.
- Breeders, traders and establishments register with the **CCSEA** (generally valid 3 years); experiments need prior approval of the CCSEA or the **Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC)**, which has **nine members** including a scientist, a veterinarian, an external member and a socially aware member.
- Use of protected wildlife, wild/stray animals and **non-human primates is restricted**, subject to scientific justification and permission.
- Which earlier rules it supersedes was not stated in the source I read; check the notification text before writing it into notes.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (animal welfare) / GS2 Governance (delegated legislation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – Environment: "Animal welfare laws"; Laxmikanth – Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A(g)). Nudge: add a table of Animal Welfare Board of India vs. the experiments committee, with legal basis for each.

articles.title: UPSC (constitutional body): Commission completes 100 years (1 Oct 1926 – 1 Oct 2026) — *PIB backgrounder, via PIB-summary sites, 19 Oct*
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** The Public Service Commission began on 1 Oct 1926 as an advisory body (Chairman and Members appointed in London). The Government of India Act, 1935 made consultation mandatory. On 26 Jan 1950 the Federal PSC became UPSC, an independent constitutional body under **Part XIV, Arts. 315–323**. Directly relevant to the merit-based civil service and the "steel frame" theme.
- **Key facts:** ICS exam introduced in London 1855; first held in India (Allahabad) 1922; Lee Commission (1924) recommended a statutory PSC; Kothari Committee (1979) gave the three-stage exam; Mains restructured to four GS papers in 2013; Universal Registration Number introduced May 2025; AI-based facial authentication used for CS (Prelims) on 24 May 2026 (about 5.5 lakh candidates). Women's share among recommended candidates rose from 6% (1952) to 31.2% (CSE 2025). Current Chairman: Dr Ajay Kumar (since 15 May 2025).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance / Polity (constitutional bodies).

articles.title: Poompuhar's seabed gives up a Mediterranean wine jar — Ancient History / Art & Culture
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The third phase of underwater exploration at Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam), by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology with the Indian Maritime University, ended on 22 Sept 2026. The finds corroborate Sangam-age maritime trade with West Asia and the Mediterranean and show a submerged city. A natural fit for GS1 (Sangam Age, Indo-Roman trade) and Prelims "ports" questions.
**Memorise.**
- A West Asian torpedo-jar fragment (30–35 cm), used to carry wine and olive oil.
- Over 250 ceramic pieces, four terracotta ring wells; read as a buried palaeochannel swallowed by the sea (about 4th–5th century CE).
- Tools: side-scan sonar, sub-bottom profiler, multibeam, ROVs.
- Poompuhar = Chola port at the Cauvery mouth; other sites to pair: Arikamedu, Alagankulam, Muziris/Pattanam.

**Notebook:** GS1 Ancient History and Art & Culture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Old (R.S. Sharma) "Sangam age"; Nitin Singhania "Ancient trade". *Nudge:* update your ports table (Poompuhar–Chola, Korkai–Pandya, Muziris and Tondi–Chera) with this find.

articles.title: The World Circular Economy Forum opens in Gandhinagar — its 10th edition and its first in South Asia — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline.** WCEF 2026 runs **15–18 September at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar**, on the theme *"Circular economy: Transition for people and prosperity"* — convened by Finland's **Sitra** with the **Central Pollution Control Board**, supported by MoEFCC and the Gujarat government. Over 2,000 participants from 65-plus countries; 125-plus exhibitors. The Board of the **10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP)** meets at Gandhinagar on 15 September, with India having recently taken over as **Co-Chair**.

**Exam angle.** Circularity is the connective tissue between SDG 12, the plastics-treaty negotiations, critical-mineral security and Mission LiFE — a single Mains paragraph can carry all four. The examiner's favourite distinction is **recycling (end-of-pipe, still linear) vs circularity (design-stage: durability, repairability, reuse, remanufacture)**, and the Indian policy instrument that operationalises it is **Extended Producer Responsibility**, which UPSC has already asked about directly.

**Facts to memorise.**

- WCEF launched by **Sitra (the Finnish Innovation Fund) at Helsinki in 2017**; 2026 is the **10th edition**, the first in South Asia.
- **10YFP** — the SCP framework adopted at **Rio+20 (2012)**, secretariat with UNEP; India now Co-Chair of its Board.
- India's architecture: **NITI Aayog's 11 circular-economy committees (March 2021)** across municipal solid and liquid waste, scrap metal, Li-ion batteries, tyres and rubber, gypsum, end-of-life vehicles, e-waste, hazardous industrial waste, used oil, agricultural waste and solar panels.
- EPR is embedded in the **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2022)**, **E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022** and **Battery Waste Management Rules 2022** — but was *first introduced* in the **e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011**.

**Notebook.** GS3 — Environment (Pollution & waste management) with a GS3 Economy spillover on resource security.

**Static anchor.** Shankar IAS *Environment* — Pollution / Waste Management chapter. *Update:* add the 11 NITI focus sectors as a memorised list, and cross-link EPR to the three waste rules plus the 2019 PYQ.

articles.title: Acharya Vinoba Bhave's birth anniversary — the land-reform movement that worked morally and failed statistically — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Prime Minister paid tribute to **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** on his **birth anniversary (11 September)** — born **Vinayak Narahari Bhave, 11 September 1895 – 15 November 1982** — the Gandhian who was hand-picked as India's **first individual Satyagrahi in 1940** and who launched the **Bhoodan movement in 1951**.

**Exam angle:** This is a **post-independence GS1 topic** that UPSC has asked in Mains verbatim (see the PYQ mirror), and the examinable argument is the gap between **moral success and structural failure**. Bhoodan was a **voluntary, non-legislative** alternative to state-led land redistribution: Bhave walked village to village asking landowners to gift land, and from **1954** escalated to **Gramdan**, the donation of whole villages into common ownership. The movement collected roughly **42 lakh acres**, but only a fraction was ever distributed — much of it was **litigated, uncultivable, or reverted** when Gramdan villages drifted back to individual title. The reason to know the numbers is that they let you make the argument precisely: voluntary transfer could not overcome **absentee landlordism, benami holdings and defective land records** — which is exactly the diagnosis that statutory **land-ceiling legislation** and, much later, **land-records digitisation** were meant to address. That gives you a live cross-link to **DILRMP 3.0** (12 September note). The second thread is **ideological**: Bhoodan is the practical arm of **Sarvodaya** and of Gandhi's **trusteeship** doctrine, and its political afterlife runs through **Jayaprakash Narayan**, who left party politics for Sarvodaya in 1954 and returned in 1974 with **Sampoorna Kranti** — a chain worth writing in one line.

**Facts to memorise:**

- **Vinayak Narahari "Vinoba" Bhave**, b. **11 September 1895**, Gagode village, **Raigad district, Maharashtra** (Konkan); d. 15 November 1982. Gandhi gave him the name **Vinoba**, placing him in the lineage of **Jnanoba and Tukoba**. Met Gandhi at **Ahmedabad, 7 June 1916**.
- **First individual Satyagrahi**, selected by Gandhi to launch the **Individual Civil Disobedience Movement, October 1940**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the second. Gandhi introduced him publicly through the essay ***"Who is Vinoba?"***
- **Bhoodan (land-gift) movement:** launched **18 April 1951** at **Pochampally village, Nalgonda district** (then Hyderabad State, now **Telangana**), where **Vedre Ramachandra Reddy** donated **100 acres** to landless Harijan families. **Gramdan** (village-gift) followed from **1954**; the first Gramdan village was **Mangroth (Uttar Pradesh)**.
- **Institutions:** **Sarva Seva Sangh** and the **Akhil Bharat Sarva Seva Sangh** carried the movement; **Gram Seva Mandal, Wardha (1934)**; earlier, the **Nagpur Flag Satyagraha (1923)**.
- **Writings:** ***Geetai*** (the Bhagavad Gita in Marathi verse, 1930–31); ***Gita Pravachane*** (18 talks delivered in **Dhule jail, 1932**); *Swarajya-Shastra*; *Sthitaprajna-Darshan*.
- **Honours:** first international **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership (1958)**; **Bharat Ratna, posthumously in 1983**.
- **Contrast to hold ready:** Bhoodan = **voluntary and moral**; **land-ceiling laws** = **statutory and coercive**, and many were placed in the **Ninth Schedule** to shield them from judicial review.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern Indian History and post-independence consolidation (social reformers; land reforms), with a GS4 spillover (trusteeship, moral persuasion as an instrument of change).

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum / Bipan Chandra — the post-independence land-reforms section; NCERT Class XII *Politics in India Since Independence*, Ch. 3 ("Politics of Planned Development").** *Update:* build a single **land-reforms ladder** — *Zamindari abolition (1950s) → Tenancy reform → Bhoodan–Gramdan (1951/1954, voluntary) → Land-ceiling legislation + Ninth Schedule → Consolidation of holdings → DILRMP/SVAMITVA (records, 2008–)* — and mark against each whether it was **voluntary or statutory** and **why it under-delivered**. **Cross-link** to your **Ninth Schedule / *I.R. Coelho* (2007)** note in Laxmikanth and to the **DILRMP 3.0** entry from 12 September.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change: India to host the World Circular Economy Forum 2026 at Gandhinagar, 15–18 September
articles.text:
India will host the **World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026** for the first time — and the first time the forum comes to **South Asia** — at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, on the theme **"Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity."** WCEF is the flagship global circular-economy convening initiated by **Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund**; the 2025 edition was held in São Paulo, Brazil. India had declared its candidacy at the 12th Regional 3R and Circular Economy Forum in Jaipur.

**Key facts**

- **Dates/venue:** 15–18 September 2026, Gandhinagar, Gujarat.
- **Co-organisers:** MoEFCC, **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, Sitra (Finland), Government of Gujarat and the **Gujarat Pollution Control Board**.
- **Scale:** over **2,000 stakeholders from 65+ countries**; an exhibition with **125+ national and international exhibitors** showcasing start-up and investment-ready circular solutions.

**Why it matters:** Links directly to Extended Producer Responsibility rules (plastic, e-waste, battery, tyre, used oil), **Mission LiFE**, the Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy agenda, and India's positioning as a Global South convener on sustainability.

**Notebook:** GS3 — Environment (waste management, resource efficiency); GS2 — IR (India as Global South convener).

articles.title: Rani Avantibai Lodhi gets a statue in Lucknow — the 1857 revolt beyond the four famous names — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline.** Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh**, with UP Chief Minister **Yogi Adityanath**, unveiled a statue of **Veerangana Rani Avantibai Lodhi** in **Lucknow on 30 August 2026**, drawing a line from the 1857 warrior queens to women officers who flew combat roles in Operation Sindoor.

**Exam angle.** UPSC's 1857 questions have moved steadily away from Delhi–Kanpur–Lucknow and toward **regional centres and their leaders** — exactly the space Avantibai occupies. Her case is also the textbook illustration of a **doctrine that is not the Doctrine of Lapse**: her husband died leaving **minor** heirs, so the Company did not annex Ramgarh outright — it placed the estate under the **Court of Wards** and installed *sarbarahkars* (superintendents), a mechanism used for minor or "incompetent" heirs. That is a distinction students routinely get wrong, and it is precisely the sort of thing a statement-based Prelims question exploits. Avantibai expelled the Company's administrators, called on cultivators to refuse British revenue demands, and coordinated with the **Gond ruler Raja Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla** through the famous **bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring chiefs and zamindars, taunting them to fight or accept the bangles. She won at the **Battle of Kheri** near Mandla against Deputy Commissioner Waddington in 1857, then shifted to guerrilla operations from the **Devhargarh** hills, and took her own life on **20 March 1858** at Sukhi-Talaiya rather than be captured. Her Mahakoshal base — Gond and farming country — is the entry point for the **tribal dimension of 1857**, which is separate from and usually more useful than the sepoy narrative.

**Facts to memorise.**

- **Maharani Avantibai Lodhi**, **16 August 1831 – 20 March 1858**; queen-regent of the estate of **Ramgarh** (present-day **Dindori and Mandla districts, Madhya Pradesh**); born at **Mankedi village, Seoni district**.
- Married **Raja Vikramaditya Singh of Ramgarh**; assumed regency for minor sons **Aman Singh** and **Sher Singh** when he was incapacitated.
- Mechanism of British seizure: **Court of Wards** with **sarbarahkars** — not the **Doctrine of Lapse** (which applied to rulers dying *without* a natural heir).
- Ally: **Raja Shankar Shah**, Gond ruler of **Garha-Mandla**, executed by the British at Jabalpur in **September 1857** along with his son **Raghunath Shah** (blown from a cannon).
- **The bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring rulers and zamindars as a challenge to join the revolt.
- **Battle of Kheri** (near Mandla, late 1857) — roughly **4,000 troops** defeated the force under Deputy Commissioner **Waddington**.
- Retreat to the **Devhargarh** hills; guerrilla strikes; encircled at **Sukhi-Talaiya** between Balapur and Ramgarh; **martyrdom on 20 March 1858**, aged 27.
- Group her with the other *veeranganas*: **Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi)**, **Jhalkari Bai** (Lakshmibai's Durga Dal commander), **Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh)**, **Rani Durgavati** (16th-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga — *not* 1857; a standard trap), **Uda Devi (Sikandar Bagh)**.
- Other 1857 centre-and-leader pairs to have cold: **Delhi — Bahadur Shah II / Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb / Tantia Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah; Allahabad — Liaquat Ali; Assam — Kandarpeshwar Singha; Orissa (Sambalpur) — Surendra Sai.**

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern History (the Revolt of 1857; significant personalities), with a GS1 Society cross-tag on women's participation in the freedom struggle.

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum — *A Brief History of Modern India*, "The Revolt of 1857"** chapter, plus the "Peasant and Tribal Uprisings" chapter for the Mahakoshal/Gond link. *Nudge: your 1857 centre-leader table almost certainly has six or seven rows. Extend it to twelve — add Ramgarh (Avantibai Lodhi), Garha-Mandla (Shankar Shah), Sambalpur (Surendra Sai), Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah) and Assam (Kandarpeshwar Singha) — and add a two-line box distinguishing the Doctrine of Lapse from the Court of Wards, since Ramgarh is a Court of Wards case, not a Lapse case.*

articles.title: BRICS Youth Council Meeting and BRICS Youth Summit held at Gandhinagar under India's 2026 Presidency
articles.text:
**Ministry/Body:** Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

As part of **India's BRICS Presidency 2026**, the Department of Youth Affairs hosted the **BRICS Youth Council Meeting** and the **BRICS Youth Summit** at **Gandhinagar, Gujarat**, a two-day event built around **'Yuva Shakti'** as a central force for innovation and sustainable development.

**Key facts**

- Participants: **official representatives, young innovators, entrepreneurs and changemakers** from BRICS **member and partner countries**.
- Purpose of the Gandhinagar leg: thematic discussions to **finalise the BRICS Youth Joint Statement** and strengthen people-to-people ties.
- **Culmination:** the **BRICS Youth Ministers' Meeting at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, on 22 August 2026**, where the **Joint Ministerial Statement on Youth Cooperation** is to be adopted.

**Why it matters:** This is the **youth track** of India's BRICS Presidency, running alongside the **Environment**, **Culture** and other sectoral tracks already convened this month — a good illustration of how a rotating presidency is actually executed through a calendar of **working groups → senior officials → ministerials**, spread deliberately across Indian cities (Gandhinagar, Visakhapatnam, Bhopal, New Delhi). Note also the standard phrasing **"member and partner countries"**, reflecting BRICS' expanded partner-country category. Notebook: **GS2 — International Relations (BRICS, plurilateral groupings)**; overlaps **GS1 — Society (demographic dividend, youth)**.

---

- **31st Southern Zonal Council meeting concluded** at Mamallapuram near Chennai under Home Minister Amit Shah — attended by the Chief Ministers of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, the Deputy Chief Minister of Telangana, and the Lt Governors of Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and the Administrator of Lakshadweep. Discussion themes: **healthcare funding, infrastructure, environmental protection and regional security**. *(Previewed on 19 August; the conclusion and participation list are what is new.)*
- **Ministry of Civil Aviation:** Minister **Ram Mohan Naidu** flagged off **transshipment cargo operations at Delhi's IGI Airport** (19 Aug) — a step towards India retaining air cargo that currently transits through foreign hubs.
- **Ministry of Finance:** Regional Rural Banks recorded **strong growth in credit delivery in 2025–26**, per a Finance Ministry release on rural credit expansion.
- **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution:** Minister Pralhad Joshi reviewed the **restructuring of the National Test House (NTH) cadre** and upgrading of its testing facilities to global standards.
- **Ministry of Education:** Minister Pralhad Joshi reviewed implementation of the PM's Independence Day announcement on **free online coaching for competitive examinations** (19 Aug); separately, the **Supreme Court** sought the Centre's response on institutionalising the **National Testing Agency** in line with the **Radhakrishnan Committee** recommendations after the NEET-UG paper leak.

articles.title: Parliament passes the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 — a 135-year-old colonial statute goes — Economy
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Rajya Sabha cleared the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 on **10 August 2026** (Lok Sabha had passed it on 5 August), completing Parliamentary passage of a law that repeals and replaces the **Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891** and gives cloud-stored and digital bank records full evidentiary standing.

**Exam angle:** A quiet but genuinely high-yield item — it sits at the junction of GS3 Economy (banking, digital financial infrastructure) and GS2 (colonial-law repeal, ease of doing business). The larger story is India's evidence law catching up with a banking system where the "book" no longer exists physically: read it alongside the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**, which already made electronic records admissible as *primary* evidence. Also a good Mains line on cutting litigation cost — banks no longer have to produce or prove physical ledgers in recovery and fraud proceedings, which matters for **DRTs, IBC proceedings and cyber-fraud prosecutions**.

**Facts to memorise:**

- Bill No. **147 of 2026**; introduced in Lok Sabha **3 August 2026**, passed LS **5 August**, passed RS **10 August 2026**. Repeals the **Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891**.
- **"Bankers' books" redefined** to cover ledgers, day-books, cash-books, account books and all records used in ordinary banking business, kept in **physical, electronic, digital or cloud-based** form — including **back-up and disaster-recovery sites**, onsite or offsite/virtual.
- Electronic/digital records are **admissible, valid and legally enforceable** subject to conditions: the system was in regular use and operating properly, no unauthorised alteration or tampering, and the network/devices were secured against cyber risk.
- **"Legal proceeding" widened** to include court proceedings, **arbitration**, and investigations/inquiries conducted under law for collection of evidence.
- **Retained safeguard:** a bank officer cannot be compelled to produce a banker's book, or appear as a witness to prove its contents, in a proceeding to which the bank is **not a party** — except by order of a court or judge made **for a special cause**.

**Notebook:** GS3 — Economy (Banking & Financial Sector Reform); cross-file in GS2 (Repeal of colonial laws)

**Static anchor:** **Mrunal — Pillar 3 (Banking / BFSI)**, banking-regulation sub-section. Add a short "evidence & recovery architecture" box, and **cross-link** it to your Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 note on Sections 61–63 (electronic records as primary evidence) so the two laws sit on one page.

articles.title: Hyderabad hosts the 2nd BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group and Asset Recovery Expert Network — International Relations
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Department of Personnel and Training is hosting the second meeting of the **BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG)** and the second meeting of the **BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery** in Hyderabad on **4–5 August 2026**, under India's BRICS Chairship of 2026. Inauguration by DoPT Secretary Ms Rachna Shah.

**Exam angle:**
- India's BRICS Chairship year is a guaranteed GS2/IR theme; the examinable distinction is **which ministry is nodal for which BRICS track** — DoPT for anti-corruption, unlike the more familiar MEA/Finance-led tracks.
- This is the "economic-offender extradition and asset recovery" theme that UPSC likes to pair with **UNCAC (2003)**, the **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018**, and Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties. Note the agenda language: cooperation is **"informal"** — i.e. agency-to-agency channels that run *alongside*, not in place of, formal MLAT/extradition routes.
- The FinTech and digital-asset corruption-risk agenda is a fresh GS3 crossover (crypto, virtual digital assets, PMLA reporting entity obligations).

**Key facts / figures to memorise:**
- Theme of India's BRICS Chairship 2026: **"Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability"**.
- Nodal department for the BRICS anti-corruption track in India: **DoPT, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.
- Three agenda pillars: (i) informal cooperation to **trace fugitive offenders** and support extradition; (ii) operational information-sharing through the **Expert Network on Asset Recovery**; (iii) corruption risks from **FinTech, digital assets and emerging digital financial instruments**.
- Side event on 5 August: **"Ethical Governance through Innovation and Tech-Driven Systems"** — digital public procurement, citizen engagement, transparency.
- Anchor treaty: **UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), 2003** — India signed in 2005, ratified in **2011**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — International Relations (Groupings & Agreements involving India); cross-file under GS4/GS2 Governance (probity, transparency).

**Static anchor:** *Laxmikanth* — chapters on the **CVC** and the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas**, plus your BRICS institutional note. **Update:** add a "BRICS working-group architecture under India's 2026 Chairship" line to the BRICS page, and cross-link the **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended 2018)** and the **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018** from the anti-corruption page.

articles.title: Second meeting of the BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group opens in Hyderabad
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (DoPT) | **Date:** 04 Aug 2026

The **2nd meeting of the BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG)** began in **Hyderabad on 4–5 August 2026**, held alongside the **2nd meeting of the BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery**. **Ms. Rachna Shah, Secretary, DoPT**, was chief guest; **Shri J. Ashok Kumar**, Chair of the BRICS ACWG, delivered the opening address.

**Why it matters:** Pair this directly with item 3 — the same policy problem (fugitive economic offenders, stolen assets, illicit financial flows) approached through a plurilateral forum. Useful for GS2 questions on "groupings and agreements involving India."

**Key takeaways**

- Core call: no jurisdiction should become a **safe haven** for those who profit from crime; deeper cooperation on **tracing fugitives, extradition assistance, and recovery of stolen assets**.
- Operationalisation of the **BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery** — a **standardised format for informal information exchange**, plus a directory of focal points and experts, to speed up law-enforcement-to-law-enforcement cooperation.
- Progress noted on the **BRICS network of law-enforcement experts** for informal cooperation in locating and extraditing corruption fugitives.
- Emphasis on **preventive vigilance and technology-driven governance** — digital identity, e-service delivery, digital payments, transparent procurement. India cited **GeM (the national public procurement portal)** and **DBT**, plus faceless and paperless taxation systems.
- Additional sessions on **ethical governance through innovation**, and on **emerging risks from FinTech and Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs)** — their misuse to conceal proceeds of corruption and launder money.

**Notebook:** GS2 — International Relations (BRICS) & Governance (transparency, anti-corruption)

articles.title: Rakhigarhi skeletons transferred to AnSI for ancient-DNA study
articles.text:
**Headline:** ASI formally handed Harappan skeletal remains from **Rakhigarhi (Haryana)** to the **Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI)** for advanced research.

**Exam angle (GS1 — Art & Culture/Ancient History):** Reinforces "Places in News" + Harappan civilisation + India's growing **ancient-DNA/bioarchaeology** capacity. Two premier Ministry of Culture bodies (ASI ↔ AnSI) under an MoU.

**Memorise:** Rakhigarhi = among the **largest Indus–Saraswati (Harappan)** settlements, in Haryana (Ghaggar plain). 2025–26 field season (ASI Excavation Branch-II) found **8 burials at Mound No. 7**; **3 complete skeletons** + fragments moved to AnSI's skeletal repository, **Kolkata**. Aim: ancestry, diet, health, migration via aDNA.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Ancient History / Art & Culture. **Static anchor:** Old NCERT *"Bricks, Beads and Bones"* / Nitin Singhania IVC chapter — add Rakhigarhi (largest site) and the AnSI ancient-DNA link.
